title: ADR: Metric ownership, volatility mitigation, and consumer contracts
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Summary

This ADR establishes a company-wide contract for metric ownership, defines mitigation patterns for metric volatility, and specifies the consumer contract for downstream telemetry users (dashboards, alerting, SLI evaluators, billing). The intent is to reduce alert noise, avoid SLO churn due to metric instability, and make metric responsibilities and lifecycle explicit.

Context

Problem statements we observed in Q4 2025 and Q1 2026:
- Dashboards show repeated spikes in the same metrics after infra rollouts, leading to noisy alerts and paging.
- Teams create ad-hoc metrics with conflicting names/semantics.
- Automated SLI producers and billing pipelines behave differently when metric cardinality or labels change, causing incorrect cost allocation.
- Backfills and metric renames often regress the availability of historical SLI evidence.

Goals
- Make metric producers accountable and discoverable.
- Reduce consumer-facing volatility (noise and SLO destabilization).
- Provide a standard contract so observability consumers can rely on stability guarantees and failure modes.

Decision (high level)

1) Metric ownership: every metric must have an explicit owner and metadata. Metadata keys required: producer-service, metric-description, unit, owner-email, cardinality-bound, stability-tier, created-via (code-review/auto). Ownership is the responsibility of the owning service team.

2) Stability tiers: metrics are assigned one of three stability tiers at creation:
   - stable: semantically fixed and backward-compatible. Allowed to be used by SLI/Billing/Customer-facing dashboards.
   - experimental: allowed in internal dashboards and alerting only with guardrails. Not allowed for long-term SLI/Billing.
   - deprecated: read-only alias pointing to a successor; expected removal timeline present.

3) Volatility mitigation patterns: recommended mitigations for high-cardinality or bursty metrics:
   - cardinality-bound enforcement (reject or sample labels beyond N unique values per minute).
   - reservoir sampling and percentile smoothing with explicit retention of raw counters for debug windows.
   - aggregated and rollup metrics with stable label sets.
   - circuit-breaker for metric emission: when a producer notices cardinality blowup, it should switch to a summarized/aggregated emission mode and emit a special metric (metric.production_mode = "aggregated") to signal consumers.

4) Consumer contract: consumers (alerting, SLI evaluation, billing) must declare which stability tiers they accept. By default:
   - SLI evaluation: stable only.
   - Billing and chargeback: stable only.
   - Internal dashboards: stable + experimental (with a per-team exception).
   - Synthetic tests and canary analysis jobs: experimental allowed but must include provenance metadata.

5) Schema and metadata: metrics must be registered in the central Metric Registry (see Implementation). Registration requires a JSON manifest with required keys (see Appendix). Attempts to use non-registered metrics in SLI rules will auto-fail CI lint.

Consequences

Positive:
- Fewer unexpected SLO regressions caused by metric renames and unbounded cardinality.
- Clear escalation path for noisy metrics: contact owner -> throttling -> temporary circuit -> deprecation.
- Billing accuracy improves because metrics used for cost allocation are explicitly stable.

Trade-offs and work required:
- Upfront overhead for teams to register metrics and add metadata.
- Some historical dashboards and scripts will need migration to registered metric names or aliases.

Implementation (step-by-step)

Owner: Observability Platform (eng-platform) + Metrics Guild representatives.

1) Metric Registry service (MRS): a lightweight service and git-backed catalog (YAML/JSON). Fields required: name, description, producer_service, owner_email, unit, stability_tier, cardinality_bound, schema_version, created_at, notes. The registry exposes an API and a CLI for registration.

2) CI Lint rule: a linter plugin for service repositories that checks for metric registration during PRs. The linter enforces naming conventions (kebab_case with service prefix) and presence of metadata. Example CI check failure message will include remediation steps.

3) Runtime producer SDK changes: open-source SDKs ingest a registry token and enforce cardinality bounds and emission modes. SDKs will emit extra diagnostic metrics when mitigation is triggered: metric.camel_case_protection_throttle_total, metric.cardinality_change_events.

4) Consumer changes: SLI evaluation pipeline will require a single config key (accepted_stability_tiers) per SLI rule. Dashboard templates will show metric stability and link to owner contact. Alerting playbooks will include a triage procedure tied to owner metadata.

5) Observability platform automation: automated email/Slack alert to owner after a metric crosses volatility thresholds (e.g., 3x median cardinality or > 10% error increase correlated with spikes).

Migration plan

1) Phase 0 (30 days): Publish registry schema, sample manifests, CI linter plugin alpha. Invite pilot teams (Runtime, Serving-runtime, SRE) to register top 200 metrics.

2) Phase 1 (60 days): SDK updates released (backwards compatible) and canary plugin applied to 25% of repos. Alerting consumers begin to require stability_tier on new SLI rules.

3) Phase 2 (90–180 days): Enforce registration in PRs for all teams (blocking). SLI/billing pipelines reject unregistered metrics for new SLI definitions. Run a migration sweep to map legacy names to registry aliases.

4) Decommission window (180–360 days): Deprecation policy enforced. Deprecated metrics maintained as read-only aliases for at least 180 days with telemetry backfill available on request.

Monitoring and SLOs for the ADR itself

We will track the rollout and effectiveness with the following measures:
- percent_metrics_registered (goal > 90% top 500 metrics within 120 days)
- metric_noise_rate (defined as alerts triggered by metric volatility patterns; goal reduce by 40% in 6 months)
- SLI_stability_incidents (number of SLI regressions traced to metric changes; target 0 after 6 months)

Alert runbook excerpt (procedural):
1. Pager receives "metric-volatility" alert with metric name.
2. Triage: consult registry -> owner_email, stability_tier, cardinality_bound.
3. If owner unreachable or mitigation not available, enable platform-level circuit: set metric emission sampling to 1/n or switch to aggregated emission.
4. Open a ticket to owner team with required remediation tasks and target remediation date.

Rollback plan

If the registry rollout causes widespread CI failures or significant developer friction, we will revert enforcement flags in CI and extend the pilot by 30 days. SDK client-side mitigations are opt-in on rollout and will be toggled via feature flags.

Open questions and future work

- How do we handle cross-service metrics where multiple producers increment the same metric? Proposed: designate a steward owning the end-to-end contract and enumerating producers in the manifest.
- Should we add automated label cardinality capping at the ingestion endpoint (edge) rather than in each SDK? Trade-off: centralized enforcement vs. producer-responsibility clarity.
- Cost model for metrics: track high-cardinality metrics with a cost center and billback to owner teams.

Appendix: Example Metric Manifest (YAML)

---
name: runtime.request.latency_ms
description: "P95 request latency for runtime endpoint (ms)"
producer_service: runtime-service
owner_email: runtime-oncall@redwood.ai
unit: milliseconds
stability_tier: stable
cardinality_bound: 50
schema_version: v1
created_at: 2026-02-10
notes: "Use runtime.request.latency_bucketed for histogram aggregations; do not add arbitrary user_id label."
---

Example CI linter output (remediation message):
"Metric registration missing for 'runtime.request.latency_ms'. Please add a manifest under /observability/metrics/<service>/ and include required fields. See: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/metric-curation-and-backfill-playbook-2025"

Ownership and governance

- Observability Platform: implement registry and automation, operate linter, manage rollout flags.
- Metrics Guild: review stability tier appeals and exception requests.
- Service teams: register metrics, respond to volatility notifications, maintain backward-compatible aliases.
